title: Writing systems of the world
examples: What is the difference between an alphabet and a syllabary?
Which writing system uses pictures as symbols?
Can you show me an example of a character writing system?

explain.say: Today we say about writing systems around the world. We will learn three main types. These are alphabets, syllabaries, and characters.
An alphabet uses letters to represent sounds. Each letter usually stands for one sound sound. English uses the Latin alphabet for writing.
A syllabary uses symbols for whole syllables. A syllable is a single unit of sound. Japanese Kana is a good example of this system.
A character system uses unique symbols for words or ideas. Chinese characters are a very famous example of this type. Each character has meaning.
In everyday life, consider writing a word like 'hello'. You use the alphabet letters. You combine them to make the sound and the word.
A common mistake is thinking all writing systems are just pictures. They are not always literal drawings of objects. They represent sounds or ideas.

draw.text: Mistake: Thinking symbols are always pictures

faq.q: How is Chinese writing different from English?
faq.a: Chinese characters are logographic, meaning each symbol often represents a whole word or idea. English uses an alphabet, where letters represent individual sounds.
asks: Do Chinese characters look like pictures?
Is Chinese writing like an alphabet?

faq.q: Does every language use an alphabet?
faq.a: No, many languages use different systems. Some use syllabaries, and others use complex character sets.
asks: Are there any non-alphabet writing systems?
What is another type of writing besides alphabet?

faq.q: What is the difference between a sound and a syllable?
faq.a: A sound is a single phonetic unit, like the 'k' in cat. A syllable is a rhythmic unit that usually contains one vowel sound.
asks: Is a syllable always one sound?
Can you give me an example of a syllable?

faq.q: Are syllabaries only used in Asia?
faq.a: While many famous examples are in Asia, the concept applies to any language structure. They group sounds into units.
Yes, writing systems evolve greatly over time. Characters can change shape or meaning across different eras.

facts: Alphabets use letters to represent basic sounds of a language.
Syllabaries use symbols representing entire units of sound called syllables.
Character systems often represent whole words or concepts, not just sounds.
The writing system used depends on the specific language spoken.

quiz.say: If a writing system uses symbols for every single sound, it is most likely:
quiz.why: Because an alphabet is defined by using letters for individual sounds.

wrong.0: While pictures are used, the term pictograph is too general for this classification.
wrong.2: A syllabary groups sounds into bigger units, not individual sounds.
wrong.3: A character often represents a whole word or idea, not just a sound.

quiz.say: Which system is best described as having symbols for whole units of sound?
quiz.why: The definition of a syllabary is that its symbols represent syllables.

wrong.0: Alphabets break sounds down into individual letters.
wrong.1: Characters usually represent concepts or words, not just sound units.
wrong.2: An abjad only writes consonants, which is a more specific type of system.

quiz.say: If a writing system uses symbols where each symbol stands for a distinct idea, it is a:
quiz.why: Character systems are known for symbolizing concepts or words directly.

wrong.1: Alphabets focus on the sounds that make up the word.
wrong.2: Syllabaries focus on the rhythmic units of sound.
wrong.3: Phonetic scripts focus on the pronunciation, not the core idea.
